You often report things that people have said or what they think. In writing, you can report their actual words in a quotation.

“I suppose you've completed the report”, she said.
He asked “What should I do now?”
Always use quotation marks when reporting direct speech or texts.
In stories or novels, it is common to place the reporting verb (say, reply, ask) before the subject when the reporting clause comes after the quotation.
“When will they be back?” asked Joe. (or, Joe asked)

Hello Denise,

Sorry I haven't written to you sooner, but it's been a bit hectic around here. The flight was relatively uneventful, and we made it to our hotel in decent time, but that's where the problems started. The hotel receptionist claimed that we didn't have a reservation, and when she finally found it, she claimed that we had only booked one room. When Adam mentioned that we had actually booked two rooms, and that we had made a few special orders, she requested that we provide a booking receipt. Fortunately we had one with us, and we were able to clear everything up. Then, at the conference, we ran into an acquaintance and ... well, that's probably a story for another day. I don't want to bog you down with unnecessary details.

The conference has been very productive. On the first day, we had a large amount of foot traffic. Our kiosk was positively swarming with potential clients. By day two, Adam pointed out that we were already running out of promotional materials and business cards. We had a sign-up sheet printed up so that those interested in receiving more information could leave their e-mail address. I really think we have made some inroads in convincing a few Midwestern writers to move their business to Boston.

I know, I harp on Adam sometimes, but he really is a great people-person. He worked the booth relentlessly, and he walked more than a few inquisitive writers through the publishing process. I'm confident that a few worthwhile leads have been generated for BFP.

Thank you again for giving us the opportunity. You can expect a full report upon my return.

Best regards,
Boris
